title: Cobblers’ Bridge
scope: Cobblers’ Bridge exterior: broad deck, five balustrade bays on either side, six pairs of tall orb columns, two shorter triple-lamp columns, geometric cornice, long central pier with two open bays and end bearings. Short quay landing aprons connect the full-width platform to the mapped bank paths.
axis: +X crosses east-northeast toward Pod Trančo; -X faces Jurčičev trg. +Z faces upstream along the Ljubljanica.

groundCutout.basis: Bridge and short landing aprons to the existing native quay paths. Buildings and transverse bank walks remain independent.

heightPolicy: Fixed 279 m model datum and approximate 284.6 m deck. The unmodified standard viewer samples 278.480 m water. Deck height, carved details, foundations and retaining interfaces are ordinary-photo approximations.
limitations: Fixed 279 m model datum and approximate 284.6 m deck. The unmodified standard viewer samples 278.480 m water. Deck height, carved details, foundations and retaining interfaces are ordinary-photo approximations.
Deck elevation and sculptural dimensions are ordinary-photo approximations. The candidate’s 273 m length is inconsistent with the retained 23.591 m crossing and is deliberately not used.
Standard urban terrain is coarse and affected by surface returns. Production approach grading and native replacement behavior have not yet been verified.
Carved capitals and balusters are stylized; lamps are static, with no lighting simulation.
The production road replacement and native approach fit are reviewed separately; this source generation does not establish readiness.
landingBasis: The retained bridge spans 23.591 m. Unobstructed short aprons connect its wide platform to native bank paths at X=-17.25 and X=15.35. Native road-height probes put both quay paths near 284.585 m across the bridge width; adjacent mapped buildings are retained.
landingRoadPolicy: Road suppression stays on the original mapped river span. Retained native approach paths carry the deck grade to the bank walks beneath the new aprons. Their paving is retained; the apron surface is about 7–9 mm above it. Expanding road suppression over the complete aprons removes the shared approach vertices and loses bank grading.
